segments.text: Welcome to the Daily Robotics Digest for November 11, 2026.
Today we cover big news, including updates on international tech deals, exciting new AI developments, and industry breakthroughs.
From Robotics & Automation News, "China blocks SoftBank’s $5.4 billion takeover of ABB Robotics".
This report details the blockage of SoftBank Group's acquisition of ABB's robotics business due to national security concerns.
The decision resulted from a review conducted by China's Office of the Working Mechanism for Foreign Investment Security Review.
The acquisition was significant because it would have granted SoftBank control over a major industrial robotics manufacturer.
Concerns were specifically raised regarding the potential transfer of robotics data and intellectual property associated with artificial intelligence training.
Despite this block, reports indicate that ABB and SoftBank are reportedly continuing discussions concerning a potential sale.
This development signals ongoing scrutiny over cross-border technology acquisitions within the industrial and artificial intelligence sectors.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, pi*0.6!".
This segment details the introduction of a new robot foundation model and its developmental status.
The model, pi*0.6, was introduced on November 17, 2025, operating at the software layer of robotics and developing using the Recap training method.
This methodology emphasizes continued training through human demonstrations, corrections, and practice.
The model currently holds a Humanoid.Guide Brain Score of four out of ten, placing it in the developing range.
Its significance is rooted in the training methodology applied to robot foundation models.
Prospective users are directed to contact the provider for information regarding access and deployment.
The advancement signals ongoing progress in the training of sophisticated robot intelligence systems.
From Humanoid.guide, Ziegler reports Gemini Robotics 2.5 use at Mercedes-Benz.
This report details the deployment of Apollo 2 humanoids on production lines in Hungary and Germany to autonomously perform automotive kitting tasks.
These robots successfully picked and sequenced metal brackets from bulk bins with a ninety-six percent success rate.
Post-training improvements demonstrated substantial results with minimal performance loss when transferred to the Mercedes-Benz production environment.

The Gemini Robotics 2.5 system supports configurations such as Apollo 2 and Franka Robotics Duo and integrates reasoning guidance for hazard avoidance and model development via simulated practice runs.
This integration signifies advancements in practical, high-precision robotic automation within the automotive sector.
From Humanoid.guide, Jens Peder Kristensen highlights NVIDIA GR00T 2 humanoid test results.
This report details performance metrics achieved by the GR00T 2 Turbo model when tested on a Unitree G1 humanoid.
During a series of forty-eight popcorn serving trials, the model demonstrated a ninety-three percent success rate in clearing tables of objects.
Furthermore, when operating onboard, the prediction time for the GR000T 2 Turbo running on the NVIDIA Jetson Thor was measured at one hundred twenty-four milliseconds.
After fine-tuning, the full model achieved a ninety-five percent success rate across fifty manipulation tasks.
Kristensen emphasized the model's potential for skill transfer derived from human demonstrations.
These results indicate progress in applying learned skills to physical manipulation tasks in humanoid robotics.
From TechCrunch - Robotics, Ring, known for its doorbell cameras, launches a home security drone and an enterprise security robot.
This report details the establishment of a new robotics division by Ring, featuring a home security drone and an enterprise security robot.
The home security drone, the Ring Drone Cam, is designed to navigate between rooms to inspect a residence and issue alerts, integrating with existing Ring devices.
The enterprise robot, the Ring Rover Cam, is equipped to patrol business routes, stream four-thousand-pixel video, and facilitate two-way audio communication.
Both devices employ a proprietary artificial intelligence system named AI Pilot for autonomous environmental mapping.
Ring has stated that the video recordings generated by these systems are secured using TAKE encryption for privacy.
This development indicates a growing trend toward deploying autonomous robotic systems in both domestic and commercial security environments.
From NVIDIA Blog, "How AI Helps Recyclers Turn Mixed Waste Into Reusable Material"
reports on the application of vision AI and robotics in sorting mixed recyclables to recover valuable materials.

This technology utilizes systems operating on conveyor belts to identify valuable materials from used clothing, bottles, and other mixed waste, resulting in the diversion of thousands of tons of materials from landfills.
The process involves AI and robotic systems that efficiently pick out recoverable items from the mixed waste stream, thereby improving the overall recycling process.
This methodology allows for the precise identification and separation of different material types within the waste.
The integration of these technologies enhances the efficiency and quality of material recovery in recycling operations.
This advancement signals the growing role of artificial intelligence and robotics in creating more sustainable material management solutions.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Improved write performance for mcap/rosbag2".
This update details write performance optimizations implemented within the mcap libraries, resulting in faster bag writing.
The improvements involved implementing optimizations within the mcap libraries, which subsequently led to an update in rosbag2 within ROS 2 Rolling to utilize these new libraries.
Consequently, the process of writing bags is now demonstrably faster than in previous versions.
Further technical details regarding these enhancements are documented in the Foxglove documentation, and the authors have opened the channel for questions and suggestions.
This advancement contributes to increased efficiency in data logging and processing within robotic and simulation environments.
From Humanoid.guide, "PRISM humanoid control module improves simulated walking".
This report details an advancement in simulated humanoid walking achieved through a new neural network input module.
The module enabled models to successfully complete ninety-two point five percent of twenty-four-second walking trials without falling.

This improvement was accomplished by allowing the models to learn multiplicative relationships among observations, past actions, and commands, providing a more explicit representation of physical interactions.
This architectural improvement yielded superior performance compared to conventional multilayer perceptrons when friction, mass, and payload were varied.

The module's effectiveness was demonstrated across diverse physical conditions without necessitating retraining, and its learned representations made quantities such as joint power and contact forces more predictable.
This development signals a step forward in the fidelity of physics simulation within artificial intelligence systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Gritt and MasTec partner to bring physical AI to solar construction sites".

This story details a collaboration where Gritt's artificial intelligence systems are being deployed on MasTec Renewables solar construction projects, successfully improving safety, efficiency, and productivity.
Gritt develops general-purpose construction intelligence utilizing robotic attachments to enhance on-site operations.
These AI systems learn physical tasks such as picking, placing, and assembly through guidance from craft employees on job sites.
The systems have demonstrated operation across various environmental conditions and actively monitor site activity to support planning efforts.
This partnership seeks to apply construction intelligence to accelerate infrastructure development through future projects.
The integration of physical AI into construction methodologies suggests a pathway for significant advancement in industrial automation.
From The Robot Report, "Why predictive maintenance matters more as factories add robots".
This report examines why predictive maintenance is more crucial as factories integrate robotic systems to ensure operational uptime and productivity.
Factories increasingly utilize robots, and this necessitates predictive maintenance to manage complex operational environments effectively.
Robotic systems generate extensive data, including measurements of vibration, temperature, and current, which serve as indicators for developing faults within the machinery.
Predictive maintenance methodologies employ this collected data, combined with contextual information from the specific workcell, to identify impending changes before actual equipment failure occurs.
This proactive detection allows maintenance teams to schedule necessary inspections precisely, thereby reducing unplanned downtime and extending the lifespan of industrial assets.
This approach facilitates proactive repairs, resulting in enhanced operational stability and greater efficiency within robotic manufacturing settings.
The integration of predictive maintenance will define the next phase of industrial automation advancements.
From NVIDIA Developer Blog, "Running AV Reasoning Models Within Onboard Compute and Latency Limits".

This report details the development of a vision-language-action model designed for real-time operation on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor, demonstrating the capability to generate chain-of-causation reasoning and driving trajectories using surround-camera observations and navigation inputs while adapting reasoning only when necessary.
The model, named NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge, was improved through closed-loop reinforcement learning within AlpaGym and evaluated using AlpaJudge for reasoning quality.

Development workflows incorporated AlpaJudge to select training examples and generate reasoning-based rewards for post-training, establishing a repeatable loop to achieve reasoning-based driving at the edge while respecting compute and latency constraints.
This advancement indicates progress in deploying complex reasoning AI directly onto automotive hardware under stringent operational limits.
From The Robot Report, Dynamic Creatures partners with Sixth Wall Studio to bring Hasbro characters to life with robots.
This story details a collaboration aimed at integrating Hasbro characters with interactive robots to create personalized guest experiences in entertainment and hospitality settings.
The collaboration merges Sixth Wall Studio's character authoring expertise with Dynamic Creatures' expressive robots.
The process involves translating a character's personality, voice, and story into physical movements and interactions executed by the robots.
This technology is designed to enable robots to greet guests, share adventures, and retain memories within venues such as theme parks, resorts, and hotels.
This integration aims to enhance guest experiences through personalized encounters.
The development signifies a growing application of advanced robotics in creating immersive, character-driven environments for commercial use.
From Humanoid.guide, Welcome, GO 3!

This report details the introduction of AgiBot's newest embodied AI foundation model, GO 3, which succeeded GO 1 and GO 2 in the Genie Operator series and achieved a Humanoid Guide Brain Score of six out of ten.
The model was developed by the Chinese humanoid robot manufacturer and is based on the WRAM framework.
Evaluation of such models necessitates separating the software from physical robotic systems and considering real-world operational requirements.
AgiBot plans to release GO 3 as open source by the end of 2026.
This development indicates progression in embodied artificial intelligence research and sets a timeline for the broader release of this technology.
From Robotics & Automation News, "How Much Work Do Robots Really Deliver? The Thinking Behind Worken".
This story details AGIBOT's proposal of Worken, a framework designed to measure the useful work robots actually complete by moving beyond simple task completion.

The framework calculates productivity using the formula involving Active Robots multiplied by Autonomous Working Hours multiplied by the Output Efficiency Ratio, which incorporates the degree of independent operation and the quality of the output against established benchmarks.

This methodology aims to evaluate the practical contribution of physical artificial intelligence in real-world environments by focusing strictly on effective work delivered rather than mere operating time.
The Worken framework provides a method to quantify robotic productivity based on achieved results.
This research signals a shift toward metrics that assess actual impact within the artificial intelligence and robotics sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, ASICS cuts inventory recovery time 60 percent using Corvus Robotics drones.
This report details how ASICS implemented autonomous inventory drones within its distribution center to enhance inventory management.
The drones increased counting frequency sixfold in high-risk storage areas, resulting in a sixty percent faster recovery of misplaced inventory.
The system utilized computer vision to accurately count items in narrow aisles, thereby reducing manual effort and improving fulfillment timelines.

This process redirected approximately two hundred hours of monthly counting labor toward inventory research and exception resolution, successfully surfacing misplaced cases and improving inventory accuracy which positively impacts revenue by enabling full-price sales.
This advancement demonstrates the tangible impact of autonomous robotics in optimizing complex logistical operations.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Greenzie autonomous mowers surpass 255,000 miles and 9 billion square feet".
This report details the operational achievements of Greenzie autonomous mowing technology, specifically noting the cumulative distance traveled and area covered by deployed systems.

The company has achieved 255,000 cumulative autonomous mowing miles and covered over nine billion square feet through commercial deployments involving more than two hundred customers across forty-five US states and four countries.
This accomplishment is facilitated by a platform designed to allow commercial mowing equipment to operate autonomously while simultaneously supporting crews and enhancing overall productivity.

Greenzie collaborates with Original Equipment Manufacturers including Wright Manufacturing, Mean Green Electric Mowers, Greenworks Commercial, and Bobcat to integrate autonomy into existing machinery and provides an adoption program to aid customer implementation.
This development indicates continued growth in the practical commercial application of autonomous systems within the grounds maintenance sector.
From techcrunch.com, "Waymo robotaxis kept illegally passing school buses after software fix, feds say | TechCrunch".
This report details an investigation by federal safety regulators concerning Waymo robotaxis that continued to illegally pass school buses following a software update.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration noted that the majority of reported incidents occurred after the company deployed the update intended to resolve the issue.
An initial investigation was triggered after video evidence showed a Waymo vehicle crossing in front of a stopped school bus in Atlanta.
Waymo stated that improvements were implemented and no citations have been issued since March 2026.
The NHTSA has subsequently opened a recall query to evaluate the sufficiency of the remedy put in place.
This situation prompts further scrutiny of autonomous vehicle deployment protocols and regulatory oversight within the technology sector.
From The Robot Report, "Intel and Altera expand collaboration to simplify sensor integration for physical AI".
This report details a collaboration between Intel and Altera to develop flexible, real-time sensor-bridge reference systems for edge and physical artificial intelligence applications.
The partnership integrates Intel's compute and software capabilities with Altera's Field-Programmable Gate Arrays to effectively manage complex data streams from various sensors.
The objective of this work is to furnish Original Equipment Manufacturers with a flexible foundation that simplifies the integration of sensing, processing, and action within real-world systems.
The development focuses on creating modular reference systems accessible via Intel's Open Edge Platform and Altera Software Development Kits.
This collaboration seeks to expedite the movement of physical AI systems from prototype to market by mitigating performance, power, and cost obstacles.
This joint effort positions the industry for more streamlined deployment of physical AI hardware.
From RoboPapers, "Ep#116: SimEX: Simulation-Integrated Robotics AutoResearch"

reports on a simulation-based auto-research framework designed to help coding agents acquire physical capabilities for controlling real robots, demonstrating that simulation is a critical component for achieving physical intelligence by enabling agents to develop knowledge and procedures.
The SimEX framework operates in two stages: initially, the agent executes open-ended probe-and-optimize iterations within simulation to develop a robot skill toolbox.

Subsequently, the agent adapts this toolbox through a limited number of physical trials, utilizing the simulation to correct the simulator and diagnose any failures encountered during real-world interaction.
This methodology allows agents to efficiently learn complex skills, such as towel folding and plate manipulation, with minimal direct physical interaction.
The research indicates that simulation serves as a vital environment for the development of necessary knowledge and procedures before physical execution.
This advancement suggests a more efficient pathway for developing advanced physical intelligence in artificial agents.
From The Robot Report, "Axon invests $1.2B into Skydio and becomes its U.S. public safety distributor".
This report details a significant investment and distribution agreement between Axon and Skydio.

Axon has invested one point two billion dollars to acquire twenty percent ownership of the drone manufacturer Skydio and will serve as the exclusive distributor for public safety entities in the United States and Canada.
This strategic partnership is designed to enhance Axon's Drone as First Responder program by integrating Skydio's artificial intelligence-backed autonomous technology.
Reports indicate that Skydio drones have demonstrated the potential to reduce public safety response times by up to sixty-five percent in certain operational deployments.
The transaction is anticipated to finalize in late two thousand twenty-six or early two thousand twenty-seven.
This development signals further integration of advanced autonomous technology within public safety operations.
From Humanoids Daily, "HD Hyundai Robotics Builds Its Own Robot Brain, as Skild AI Pitches Korea on Building the Bodies".
This report details the development of a robot with an in-house foundation model and the subsequent proposal by Skild AI to Korean hardware manufacturers for robot bodies.

HD Hyundai Robotics developed a robot featuring dual-arm hands equipped with five-fingered grippers, which operates initially on a wheeled base for kitting before expanding to welding and painting functions.
The company's AI agents demonstrated efficiency improvements, reducing problem resolution time from twenty-one point five days to seven point nine days.

Skild AI is currently seeking collaborations with Korean motor and actuator makers to supply the necessary hardware components for its robot models, positioning Korea as a source capable of integrating with established Korean manufacturing capabilities.
This development signals an increasing focus on integrated hardware and advanced artificial intelligence in industrial robotics.

From Robotics & Automation News, Oversonic Robotics takes the RoBee R20 humanoid robot to Munich and Lisbon, demonstrating the company's expansion into the international market for its specialized humanoid technology.
Oversonic Robotics specializes in designing and manufacturing cognitive humanoid robots in Italy, developed on a platform combining artificial intelligence and human-robot collaboration.
The RoBee R20 robot is engineered to assist workers in industrial tasks such as picking and handling within environments meeting ISO Class 6 control standards.
This international exposure serves to position Italian robotics solutions globally by showcasing specific expertise in the evolving humanoid robotics sector.
This initiative supports the objective of demonstrating Italian capabilities in the rapidly advancing field of humanoid robotics.
The international presentation signals a growing focus on advanced collaborative robotics solutions across global industrial applications.
And that's all the circuits for today.
From global robotics shifts to that big takeover, keep those algorithms running smoothly.
Until tomorrow, keep building amazing things!
Bye for now.
